# Light Field Representation


## Overview
Light field representation is a technique that generates a high-quality parameterization of the light field and integrates it into a GPU-based raycasting pipeline to provide novice audiences with access to interactive volume renditions [S1]. It builds on [Light Field and Lumigraph Methods](9271-light-field-and-lumigraph-methods.md) and differs from sibling methods like [Local Light Field Fusion](1124-local-light-field-fusion.md) and [Neural Lumigraph Rendering](7369-neural-lumigraph-rendering.md) by prioritizing real-time [GPU raycasting](#6192-gpu-raycasting.md) integration for novice users over neural optimization or local fusion [G].

## Subtopics

### [Two-plane light field parameterization with re-parameterization](16989-two-plane-light-field-parameterization-with-re-parameterizat.md)
This method parameterizes a light field using two planes, $\pi_{xy}$ and $\pi_{uv}$, and learns a re-parameterization (local affine transforms) to align the neural network's [interpolation kernels](#21073-spatial-resampling-and-interpolation.md) with the object surface $\pi_{st}$. It solves the problem of misaligned interpolation kernels in standard [two-plane parameterizations](#16989-two-plane-light-field-parameterization-with-re-parameterizat.md), which degrades view synthesis quality when the distance between the view plane and the object surface is large. It sets itself apart from standard two-plane methods by explicitly optimizing the embedding space to minimize the discrepancy between the parameterized coordinates and the true surface coordinates.
